title: Matrix-Induced Cancellations and Degree-Bound Tightness
summary: The coefficient-grouping bound may be non-tight when the affine-layer matrix changes monomial coefficients; characterizing those cancellations and their impact on tightness remains open.

formal_statement.body: Characterize cancellations induced by $M$ over $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ and determine their effect on the tightness of the algebraic-degree upper bound.

scope.domain: Algebraic-degree analysis of coefficient grouping for affine layers in symmetric cryptography.
parameters: $M$: the invertible matrix whose changes to monomial coefficients can induce cancellations
$n$: determines the finite-field size and the range of possible coefficient values
scope.unresolved_remainder: Characterize the monomial cancellations induced by $M$ over $\mathbb{F}_{2^n}$ and determine their effect on upper-bound tightness.

citations.label: Coefficient Grouping for Complex Affine Layers

progress.summary: The source omits the influence of $M$ in its coefficient-grouping analysis by setting all possible monomial coefficients to 1, and warns that some choices of $M$ may make the upper bound non-tight. It explicitly presents detecting the resulting cancellations as an open problem.
citation_labels: Fukang Liu et al., Coefficient Grouping for Complex Affine Layers
